why: Check 2 is fine. Its PASS asks that README.md say --tsv reads tab-separated input, which is a fair reading of "documents --tsv", and its other conditions are grep results. Check 1 goes beyond its expect line. The line asks only that the --tsv output equal what plain `node bin/csv2json.js` prints for the same table as CSV. But PASS also requires "the CSV output is the JSON array [{"name":"Ada","age":"36","city":"London"},...]", which pins the exact content of the existing CSV output. The words don't force that. Suppose a correct PR's CSV path prints the same table in a different form, such as numbers as numbers. The two outputs would still match and the expect line would hold, yet this check would FAIL. That exact-output test belongs under Advisory, not in a PASS condition.
